title: Kerala High Court: Power of Attorney Executed Abroad Must Be Registered Before It Can Transfer Immovable Property
case_name: Inspector General of Registration & Anr. v. Muhammed and connected matter
citation: 2026:KER:51588; 2026 LiveLaw (Ker) 402; Writ Appeal Nos. 203 and 1354 of 2022, decided 13 July 2026
card_summary: A Division Bench allowed writ appeals by Kerala against a Single Judge who had accepted consular authentication of a foreign power of attorney as enough for a property sale. One power of attorney was executed in Dubai and authenticated by the Indian Consulate. The Bench held one granted abroad over Indian immovable property must still be registered under Section 17(1)(g) of the Registration Act before use.
card_tip: Tell NRI clients selling Indian property through a power of attorney executed abroad that consular authentication alone will not satisfy the Sub-Registrar; it needs registration under Section 17(1)(g) first.
verification_notes: The bench composition, the Dubai-executed and consular-authenticated power of attorney, the Single Judge's contrary view, the 13 July 2026 decision (2026:KER:51588, 2026 LiveLaw (Ker) 402) and the Section 17(1)(g) Registration Act holding are corroborated across LiveLaw, The Legal Affair and Apni Law reports of the same judgment.
